items.title: Update README.md: add `list` to the documented command list and to the pinned usage line, and document the --json flag.
Assert the list output order without sorting, so criterion 53.1's 'in that order' is actually pinned by a test.
README.md still documents the pre-epic CLI contract
items.detail: README's `## CLI` section states `Commands: greet, cheer, farewell, motto, version, all.` and pins the exact usage line without `list`. Both are now false on this branch, and --json is undocumented there. README is the repo's stated CLI contract and the test file's own comment cites it as such.

items.title: The list test sorts, so the required output order is never asserted
items.detail: Criterion 53.1 requires the six names 'one per line, in that order'. The test compares [...names].sort() against a sorted constant, so reordering src/list.js leaves the suite green. Its comment also claims it catches an unlisted command, but it would instead fail if list ever listed itself.

items.title: A new test asserts `node src/cli.js list` exits 0 and prints the expected command names, one per line.

summary: Both underlying defects were real and are fixed. README's ## CLI section now lists `list` in the commands sentence and the pinned usage line, and documents --json with a verified example (F1/F3, the same defect stated twice). The list smoke test now asserts the six names in order via a LIST_ORDER constant instead of comparing sorted arrays, and the membership cross-check against the suite's file list was rewired to compare LIST_ORDER to the files so its comment is finally true (F2/F4, same defect; F5's criterion 55.3 goes from partial to met by the same change since the test now asserts exit 0 plus the expected names one per line in order). Verified the new assertion actually bites by reordering src/list.js and watching the suite fail, then restoring it. `node src/greet.js` exits 0 and the full suite is 15/15. Nothing deferred; no adjacent code touched.

fixed.detail: Criterion 55.3 is now fully met: the existing test asserts exit 0 and, after this change, the exact expected names one per line in order rather than as an unordered set.
